comment.body:
Ha! Nice try. If you're implying that anyone who doesn't see or interpret reality the same way you do is psychotic, that's not gonna fly. There's a huge spectrum of understanding and interpretation available within the realm of "reality" and the enormous body of data available to humans today. None of us have the whole picture. I doubt any human brain has the actual capacity, nor does any individual have the years of life to cram their brain full of all that data.

You can shout into your bullhorn about how you see the world all you want (and that's the freedom I'm talking about) but it's still just one person seeing one picture through the lens they have available from their body of experience, accumulated knowledge, and (trained or untrained) ability to analyze and form opinions.

I appreciate that people are sharing what they see. I recognize that you and I see very differently, but I'm still glad you're sharing your bit. It's by sharing each of our perspectives that we have the opportunity to glimpse things outside what we'd discover or think of on our own. 

You may or may not value what I see or have to share, and that's okay. That's something you're free to choose, too. :-)

comment.body:
Regarding "freedom to believe what you want, and me the freedom to believe what I want"—sorry. No one in the world has that "freedom" if it means "whatever I want to believe, period, without considering what's really going on." I'm not saying a person doesn't have the freedom to jump off a cliff, let's say. I'm saying that their freedom to jump doesn't give them freedom from the consequences of jumping.

Everyone, for example, has the freedom to hallucinate. But they don't have the freedom to take their hallucination and "believe" it as if it were the truth.

So, no, you don't have the freedom to believe what you want unconstrained by reality, because breaking from reality constitutes psychosis. You and I reside in the same universe, so that's our common ground. It isn't subject to what we want to believe, and it doesn't change simply because we want to believe X, Y, or Z about it. Strictly speaking, you even have the freedom to be psychotic. But why would you want to? In other words, neither of us has the freedom to escape from the real situation we find ourselves in: residing in the same shared universe. That's why we call breaking from it "psychosis".

comment.body:
I get where you're coming from, but I think it's hard to deny that millennia of human history point to a consistent human nature that is programmed to violence, that admires strength, that relishes fire-cooked meat, is tribal, territorial, and a lot of things that we abhor about the picture painted in the Old Testament writings. I mean... I don't get all the blood and gore of it all, either. But if the apostle Paul was right, and the Old Covenant was just a way of making sure the whole universe bears witness to the fact that the New Covenant is WAY better... 

When Jesus came along, he shined more light on the intentions and nature of God. I can see that the two beings "the God of the OT" and "Jesus' Father" seem totally different on the surface, but.... as a parent, I see similarities -- and it reminds me of what happens when raising children. 

When left to itself, human nature is selfish and takes whatever it wants, whenever it can. Babies and toddlers are incredibly demanding. When guided and disciplined by parents, children learn to master their emotions, their desires, their inclination toward selfishness and immediate gratification. But nearly always at some point in the process, the children think they "hate" the parent, because they don't understand why they can't have what they want NOW.

If I put myself in the shoes of a God who created humanity and allowed freedom to choose good or evil -- so that the LOVE of the human spirit would also be freely given and not just programmed or forced -- then I'm in a tough place. How do you get your point across to mortal beings like us? Humans who so easily fall into choosing whatever makes them feel good, even at the cost of others? While it's easy for me to think I'd do things differently, it's also relatively easy for me to grasp that Someone might choose to let history unfold the way it has in the interests of some Bigger Picture. Not just for our sake, but probably for Reasons Beyond Us.

And maybe this is too much of a stretch for most folks, but as a fiction writer, it's clear to me that a story wouldn't sell if there wasn't action, angst, yearning, aspiring, tragedy, courage, sacrifice, transformation, adventure, betrayal, and all the rest. When I write a story, the readers don't generally complain that I hurt the characters too much. And if they do, the obvious answer is, "It's my story, I get to do whatever I want with it." If we're truly the creations of a Creator, then hey... he gets to do whatever he wants with us. And if we're so full of ourselves and our ability to judge our Creator that we say "You have no right!" or "That's not fair!" or "That makes you a monster!" then... /shrug/  

Hey, he's given us the freedom to say that.

Given you the freedom to believe what you want, and me the freedom to believe what I want. It seems to me that the life we live here on earth is designed to teach us things we'll need for life Elsewhere. Thus, I observe that we may need to understand the proper use of power (including us of force / violence), and the pitfalls of using it for selfish purposes... as well as the benefits of using it to bring peace and protection against other force / violence. We need to understand the power of faith, and how to believe in what we don't yet see in order to bring it about. We need to value relationship and value ourselves and see how those things all fit together to make mutually beneficial connections. So much to learn and practice while we're here...

comment.body:
I’m not denying anything. What I’m doing is not taking that history out of context. The millennia of human history that you say show a consistent human nature that is programmed to violence amounts to about 0.25% of the data required for a **minimally adequate** sample for the purpose of forming a theory about “human nature”. It’s like basing a theory of the nature of human skin on a pimple. Here’s the convo link if you’re interested: https://copilot.microsoft.com/shares/mu5fPHYR6V182YdS9nmts

Here’s the upshot:

Me:	Make a statement about basing theories about "human nature" solely on the recorded history of homo sapiens compared to the minimum adequate sample you've outlined.

Copilot:	Basing theories of "human nature" solely on the ~0.25% sliver represented by recorded history of Homo sapiens is statistically indefensible. It ignores 2 million years of behavioral data across multiple Homo species, geographic zones, and ecological contexts—rendering any conclusions drawn from such a narrow slice profoundly biased and anthropocentrically myopic.

But it’s worse than that. I asked it how many person-days represented in recorded history was devoted to violence. Less than 0.5%.

So the “violent human nature” claim rests on 0.5% of 0.25% of the total human experience: 0.00125%.

Me:	So, the evidence for human violence rests on 0.5% of 0.25% of the human experience overall, correct?

Copilot:	Correct. The empirical basis for claims about human violence—if drawn solely from recorded history and violent activity within it—represents approximately 0.00125% of the total behavioral experience across the Homo genus.

Me:	So, how can people say that violence is a major feature of human nature?

Copilot:	Because they conflate visibility with prevalence. Violence is overrepresented in recorded history due to its dramatic, disruptive nature—wars, crimes, and political upheavals dominate written records. But statistically, violence occupies a minuscule fraction of human behavior across time. The claim reflects sampling bias, not empirical proportion.

I won't take the time to go into the rest of the myths of human nature you mentioned. They are similarly fallacious.

Bottom line: humans behave differently under different conditions. Violence results under certain conditions (external and internal) and not others. Yes, it is human nature to become violent under those conditions. But what about the hugely more plentiful conditions under which human nature is cooperative, mutually supportive, loving, and constructive? The human nature views you've echoed deny all that. 

There's one more level to this: natural conditions vs. human-caused conditions. You’ll see in the convo that Copilot estimated the relative difference between violence rates prehistory vs. historical: 

Estimated prevalence of violence (person-days):

•	Prehistoric (pre-5,000 years ago): Violence-related person-days ≈ 0.05% Peaceful person-days ≈ 99.95%

•	Historical (last ~5,000 years): Violence-related person-days ≈ 0.5% Peaceful person-days ≈ 99.5%

This suggests that historical humans experienced 10× more violence per capita than prehistoric humans.

Here are the conditions that changed, and ALL of them are human-caused—so, they can be human-corrected:

Me:	So, major factors must have changed between than and the period of recorded history.

Copilot:	Yes. Key shifts include:

•	Agriculture and sedentism: Resource accumulation led to territoriality and inequality.

•	State formation: Centralized power enabled organized warfare and coercive control.

•	Population density: Increased competition and anonymity reduced kin-based cooperation.

•	Written records: Violence became more visible through documentation, amplifying its perceived prevalence.

•	Ideological systems: Religion, nationalism, and hierarchy justified and ritualized violence.

These structural changes transformed sporadic conflict into systemic violence.

So, this supports that the OT is a corrupt view of humanity, because it falsely represents conditions and violent results which are of human origin as if they were “natural”, and it pretends that conditions unique to 0.00125% of human experience applied to the whole—DENYING the vast majority of conditions resulting in violence-free experience that were the case for almost the whole experience span of the genus. 

Not only is that wrong, it’s so hugely wrong that it’s fair to call it psychotic in the literal and simple sense: bullshit taken for real due a severe psycho-social break from reality.

Overall, this brings us right back to the "where is the truth" question. It's not in the words on the page. The truth is what those words *refer to*. The truth exists only in consciousnesses capable of perceiving what's really going on AND self-aware enough to check their own perceptions and detect disconnections between their perceptions and what their perceptions inform them about. That's why the "word of truth" (as God is truth) is living and active. It doesn't stand still. It stays intimately connected to what's really going on as it happens and as things change. The words on the page are at best a map, not the territory.

As far as the Israelites, I've thought about this now for almost 60 years. (I became a born-again, spirit-filled Christian at 17, but my ponderings on Christ and Christianity began around 12 years old.) The reason God (if it actually was God -- Gnostics would disagree) "chose" Abraham and his descendants was that he couldn't find a more psychopathic group of human beings to work with. If the God of the Jews was every bit the psychotic, genocidal, brutal, bloodshed-loving ghoul that the Jewish writings portray him to be, he was the devil, just like the Gnostics claim. A being that finds the smell of burning feathers, fur, and flesh a "soothing aroma"??? Give me a fucking break. Have you ever smelled that odor? A being that finds that stink soothing isn't anything I'm going to respect, let alone "worship".

Or if, as Christians believe, the God of the Jews was the same being as Jesus' Father, then the OT writings describe what happens when psychopaths interact with God. They simply cannot fathom a god that isn't "all powerful" when their only concept of "power" is **violent might**: the capability to destroy, annihilate, and extort by means of the threat of destruction and annihilation. 

Sorry, any "god" that distinguishes itself by superiority in power-as-violence is absolutely not the god of Jesus or of John, who wrote "God is love". 

Either way, the devil as god or the god that psychopaths bastardized and corrupted into a genocidal devil, the OT writings are valuable and instructive, but they are in no way a reliable map of the truth, not as is. The ideas in it need to be reverse engineered to be valuable, eliminating the beast mind that originated them and which they reflect.

comment.body:
Well, to be fair, when God gave the Israelites instructions, he directed them to be written down and taught to each generation. He said his words and ways were so essential that they should be put in your heart and kept before your eyes and meditated on. So after that, the written word of God was referenced that way and his instructions to learn and keep in their hearts those words were referenced. When men added to that collection of written words, they applied the same concept to the new words as God instructed originally. 

I think it makes perfect sense that when God speaks to us -- when he communicates, in whatever ways that he chooses (the written testimony of his words to someone else, dreams, visions, pointing out natural things around you in ways that offer wisdom for your life and action steps, through the words of others as he inspires them, etc) -- that we should pay attention and remember those things. Maybe write them down, if we're prone to forgetting. Ink on a page isn't bad by itself. It's when someone else's ink is being forced onto my life that it gets problematic.

Sometimes a revelation becomes a north star that keeps us focused and centered for the rest of our life. Sometimes it's a seasonal or progressive revelation and just a signpost on a path behind us that's superseded by new directions once we reach the place it was directing us.

comment.body:
Kind off the ReLOVEution topic—except failures of clear thinking are always well in scope—but a couple of memes that show how dumbshit thinking can persist among even our best and brightest for centuries without anyone seeming to notice.

The first is the culmination of a gnarly convo with Grok which I finally got straightened out: 

NO direct empirical evidence for the HISTORICAL ACTUALITY of macroevolution. 

Direct empirical evidence we have supports the POSSIBILITY that macroevolution occurred the way we conceive of it.

Trenchant conflation of possibility and actuality ever since Darwin’s time.

The second was my eensy “holy shit!” this morning. 😁

ReLOVEution would be the natural, unavoidable result of people simply being honest, thinking clearly, and paying attention to what’s really going on inside them and around them.

Just look at how much work it’s taking me to think it through myself and articulate it!

My friends, we were MASSIVELY mindfucked. 

Rabbit holes are the result of trying to dig our way out of the mountains of lies, bullshit, and gaslighting we were buried under. Escape doesn’t come magically or instantly, and there are no magic keys or silver bullets. Just honesty, love of the truth, and a shitload of deconstruction work.

This is why Nietzsche recommended doing philosophy with a hammer. Now, after well more than a century of additional PhDs (pile it higher and deeper) buffaloing us, it’s gonna take a sledge hammer… if not a jackhammer.

https://grok.com/share/c2hhcmQtMg%3D%3D_16e2655e-25cf-4cd0-a6fd-545fab81d2ce

comment.body:
Finally, we're actually talking about it.

The order of magnitude difference between the criminality you think the government is supposed to protect you from and the criminality of the government itself is mammoth.

Ruled by psychotic elephants to "protect" you from mice.

So, who is more psychotic than whom?

Who believes the lie that "authority" is legitimate?

Codependents.

Who not only don't need "authority" to keep them in line, but suffer it as full frontal assault?

Human beings.

Am I saying that codependents are not human beings?

Biologically, they're human beings.

Psychologically, they're subhuman.

Their minds, identities, and their very souls have been dehumanized.

I agree with her solution. It's easier and simpler than almost everybody thinks.

Stop being codependent, demanding that something or someone must enable you to survive and live a minimally tolerable life.

Start being self-enabling.

That's it.

That's the "strait gate" to the "narrow way" that leads to life. The gate is not the way, and the way is not the life. The life comes as a direct result of going through the gate and walking on the way.

True humanity is FERAL. So, in that light, you know now what "civilization" actually means.
